entry_conditions: Supported earliest takeover is unfinished red descent over the pad, not an already completed red subgoal. Across measured starts, d is approximately 0.300 m, red/TCP z approximately 0.211/0.212 m, each finger approximately 0.0182 m (summed width approximately 0.0365 m), and blue z approximately 0.020 m outside the drawer. Later supported takeovers include red release, empty upward retreat/transit, blue approach with open fingers, closure beside blue, and initial lift toward blue z approximately 0.14 m. The two causal observations expose qpos[0:9], qvel[9:18], TCP pose[18:25], red pose[25:32], blue pose[32:39], drawer position[39] and velocity[40]. Positions are world-frame metres and quaternions wxyz. Relative TCP-object positions, heights, per-finger openings, qvel and inter-observation displacement distinguish these phases. Closed fingers plus a nearby block moving with TCP suggest grasp, but are not contact measurements. These are observed-support descriptions, not strict applicability thresholds or a requirement for a source-index-based handoff.
exit_conditions: Use exactly the simultaneous completion contract on actual observations: d>0.26 m; red center z in the open interval (0.014,0.031) m; blue center z in (0.053,0.074) m; abs(red_xy-[-0.18,-0.30])+red_extent_xy <= [0.06,0.06]; abs(blue_xy-[0.19-d,0])+blue_extent_xy <= [0.172,0.182], where extent_i=0.02*sum_j abs(R_ij) from each block's wxyz rotation. One observation suffices. Blue at z approximately 0.067 m can satisfy this while fingers remain closed, as observed at demo1000:980, demo1001:990 and demo1008:985. No release, speed, dwell or clearance requirement is added. Useful retained endpoints have d approximately 0.2973-0.2974 m, red near [-0.176 to -0.177,-0.298 to -0.304,0.020] m and blue near [-0.1717 to -0.1728,0.0728 to 0.0742,0.063] m; these ranges are context, not additional constraints.
overlap_role: The entire assigned expanded slice is learned, including the 270-278 shared actions with evacuate_red in each demonstration. For example the common actions are [575,845) in demo1000, [581,859) in demo1001 and [575,853) in demo1008. They teach red descent/release, empty retreat and approach to blue, blue closure and initial lift. This policy retains both object tokens and all red margins at all times: it must finish incoming red placement when necessary and preserve red thereafter while manipulating blue. It neither discards the overlap nor assumes that changing the option name implies red success. Two-frame causal motion cues allow partway takeover without restarting a scripted phase sequence.
successor_readiness: No downstream manipulation policy is required once the simultaneous task contract is satisfied. The task monitor may accept success even if blue is still grasped. If transitioning to optional idle after learned continuation, inspected suffixes provide red and blue remaining in their spatial goals, d approximately 0.297 m, per-finger opening near 0.04 m (total near 0.08 m), and an empty TCP retreated to z approximately 0.323 m. These are useful observed successor context, not necessary success conditions. Red-on-pad alone can hold during empty retreat and blue acquisition; it is not a final task exit. Likewise, blue near the TCP with closed fingers does not alone establish successful acquisition; coordinated rising blue/TCP is stronger but still inferred grasp support.
failure_signatures: Center-inside with any negative full-containment XY margin is not containment. Blue center z>=0.074 m or <=0.053 m, red center z outside its strict interval, d<=0.26 m, or red leaving full pad containment prevents simultaneous completion. Lack of release alone is not failure. Closed fingers near a blue block that remains outside on the surface while TCP rises can suggest a missed grasp; separation or falling blue can suggest loss. Those are observation-based diagnostics, not implemented recovery rules or guaranteed contact tests. Materially displaced red or unexpectedly closing drawer calls for external reassessment because recovery is not established by these demonstrations.
continuation_guidance: Continue this policy while completing the incoming red descent/release, empty transition, blue acquisition, transport and insertion if observations remain consistent with demonstrated support and the simultaneous contract is not yet true. Replan using the fixed sampler and aligned eight-action prefix, not a preset skill schedule. A transition to this policy need not wait for red release or initial blue lift: the overlap explicitly covers earlier phases. Once the simultaneous contract holds, stopping is permitted immediately; if useful, optional continued invocation learns blue release, settling and upward empty retreat from the retained suffix. Do not require that optional suffix for accepting task success. The auxiliary future-margin predictions are internal training supervision, not deployment acceptance scores or a safety certificate.
limitations: The learned transformer produces original-shared-normalized absolute joint/gripper actions. It has no IK, contact sensor, image encoder, collision checking, external candidate scoring, phase controller or replay. Geometry uses the fixed supplied world-frame contract; changed geometry needs a revised contract. Quaternion-sign ambiguity is removed but spatial equivariance is not asserted. Training largely shows near-upright, interior placements and almost fully open drawers. Measured boundaries/overlap provide support only, not proof of policy success, exact grasp state, edge-placement robustness or recovery from unexpected disturbances. Two observations cannot disambiguate every stationary holding phase.
